content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"CI/CD Pipelines for NativeScript Apps"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) automate the building, testing, and releasing of your NativeScript applications. This tutorial explores setting up an automated pipeline using GitHub Actions to compile and deploy your cross-platform mobile apps efficiently."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A working NativeScript project hosted in a GitHub repository."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Basic knowledge of YAML syntax and GitHub Actions."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"App Store Connect and Google Play Console accounts for final deployment stages."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Create the GitHub Actions Workflow Directory"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"In your root project directory, create the necessary folder structure for GitHub Actions workflow files."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"mkdir -p .github/workflows"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Configure the Workflow File"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create a file named 'ci.yml' inside the '.github/workflows' directory. This file defines the steps to setup the environment, install dependencies, run tests, and build the application."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"name: NativeScript CI\\n\\non:\\n  push:\\n    branches: [ main ]\\n  pull_request:\\n    branches: [ main ]\\n\\njobs:\\n  build:\\n    runs-on: macos-latest\\n    steps:\\n    - name: Checkout Repository\\n      uses: actions/checkout@v3\\n\\n    - name: Setup Node.js\\n      uses: actions/setup-node@v3\\n      with:\\n        node-version: '18'\\n\\n    - name: Install NativeScript CLI\\n      run: npm install -g nativescript\\n\\n    - name: Install Project Dependencies\\n      run: npm install\\n\\n    - name: Run Build for Android\\n      run: ns build android --bundle"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Managing Environment Variables and Secrets"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"To sign your apps for production, you must store your keystores (Android) and provisioning profiles/certificates (iOS) securely inside GitHub Repository Secrets."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Go to your GitHub repository settings."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Navigate to Secrets and variables -> Actions."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Add sensitive data like ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64, KEYSTORE_PASSWORD, ALIAS_PASSWORD, and KEY_ALIAS."},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Automating Deployment"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Extend your workflow to deploy the built binaries to Google Play and Apple App Store using Fastlane or dedicated GitHub Actions for mobile distribution."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"- name: Deploy to Google Play\\n  uses: r0adkll/upload-google-play@v1\\n  with:\\n    service_account_json_file_path: service_account.json\\n    release_file: platforms/android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk\\n    track: production"},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"By implementing this CI/CD pipeline for your NativeScript application, you ensure that every commit is tested and built consistently, significantly reducing manual errors and speeding up release cycles."}]
